cases.catches: if fs.read stopped being served for a relative sandbox path, this case fails: the program takes its ok branch only when the call is served and returns ok
a missing file is a program-visible err, not a host crash and not a widened path
a parent-directory path is refused even when the file exists just outside the sandbox root
an absolute path is refused before any filesystem access, so the sandbox root is never bypassed
a file larger than the 1 MiB output budget is refused as err instead of being read into the guest
if fs.write stopped writing inside the sandbox, the granted case would stop producing the file
a parent-directory write is refused and no file appears outside the sandbox root
an absolute write path is refused, so the write side is not weaker than the read side; the after-state proves no file appeared beside the sandbox
the stdout budget is observable: a small write reaches program_stdout and exits 0
a write above the 1 MiB budget is refused, and the refused bytes never reach program_stdout
if process.args stopped being served or stopped returning ok, this case fails; the empty argument list itself is host configuration recorded in 4.2, not asserted here
a policy that grants nothing still lets a builtin capability run: the policy is not a sandbox for the builtin surface
naming a builtin capability in a policy is refused as not-served instead of silently widening or narrowing it
the write side is refused the same way, so the not-served rule is not read-only-specific
a process status outside 0..=255 is refused at compile stage, before the host is reached
the third served declared member (clock) runs end to end once registry and policy agree
a registry that declares clock does not grant it: without the grant the run is refused as a capability failure
a family a registry declares but this toolchain does not serve is refused as not-served instead of reaching a host adapter
without a registry the declared reference never resolves, so no declared call can be reached from source text
an artifact compiled once by `compile` still runs under the policy that grants its member
the same artifact under a policy that does not grant the member is refused, so the artifact carries no authority of its own
the registry alone never authorizes a run: without a policy the artifact is refused as policy-missing
